component.name: Travel Log
component.summary: Location history and tracking for Dawarich

description.p: Travel Log works with your own Dawarich server, on a Phosh phone and on the desktop. It will show where you have been on a map and record your phone's position for your server.
This first version is only the empty app; connecting to a server comes next.
Travel Log is an independent project and not affiliated with Dawarich. Your location data goes only to the server you configure.

ul.li: "Report a Problem…" in the main menu sends your problem or idea to the developers as a GitHub issue, with your own token or through GitHub's issue form in the browser.
Connect to your Dawarich server with your e-mail and password (including two-factor codes) or an API key, kept in the keyring.
Tracking goes on with the window closed and the phone asleep, resumes after a restart and can start at login.
A sidebar shows the day's distance, time moving and visits; tap a visit to find it on the map.
See the tracks and visits of a day on the map and move between days.
Export the points recorded on your phone for a day as a GPX file.
A map of OpenStreetMap with a button to show your own location.
Days you have opened are saved, so they show without network too.
See a whole week or month on the map; the calendar marks the days that have data.
Statistics: distance per year and month, and the countries and cities you visited.
A notification shows while your location is recorded, with a button to stop.
Tracking settings: how often to record, where to send points (your Dawarich account or any Overland or OwnTracks server) and how long to keep them, shared with your other devices through Dawarich.
Record your position while Travel Log is open and upload it to your Dawarich server or another Overland or OwnTracks server; today's track grows live on the map.
Confirm, decline or rename visits and choose their place, with Undo.
Clear messages for days without data, an unreachable server, a rejected key and a server that is too old.

description.p: First version: the empty app, ready to install, without a server connection yet.
